title: sunset-legacy-embeddings-draft
content:
Purpose
- Draft internal announcement + Q&A for sunsetting the legacy embeddings endpoint (v1/embeds-legacy) and nudging customers toward the new Embeds V2 pipeline.
- This is a working scratchpad: rough talking points, migration guidance, known risks and open questions.

High-level summary (for exec/all-hands line)
- We plan to retire the legacy embeddings endpoint on 2026-05-15.
- Reason: Embeds V2 provides 4–6x better throughput, lower cost per vector, and improved accuracy for long contexts; keeping both paths is increasing maintenance and operational risk.
- Migration window: 60 days of overlap, tooling + incentives to migrate early.

Audience breakdown
- Internal (CS, Solutions, Sales, Support, SRE, Eng): need a clear runbook and escalation path.
- Early adopter customers: dedicated outreach + migration support.
- Remaining customers: in-product notices, migration guide, automated SDK helpers.

Draft internal announcement (short)
- Subject: Planned retirement of legacy embeddings endpoint (v1) — timeline & migration help
- Body: 
  - TL;DR: We will deprecate v1/embeds-legacy on 2026-05-15. Embeds V2 is faster, cheaper, and the default for new workloads. Overlap period and migration tooling will be provided; CS/SE will get a migration kit.
  - Why: maintenance cost, accuracy improvements, and unified perf/security profile across Dedicated/Private/Hosted.
  - Ask: Support teams prepare FAQs, update runbooks, and flag any customers with custom integrations.

Talking points for customer conversations (CS / Solutions)
- Benefits to emphasize: lower latency, reduced per-request cost, fewer retries, and first-class batching support.
- Migration steps (short): update SDK to v3.1+, switch to endpoint /v2/embeddings, opt-in to "preserve-dimensions" flag only if you rely on exact vector dims, run compatibility check using our migration tool (link).
- If a customer cannot migrate before sunset: offer temporary Dedicated lanes or a 90-day emergency extension (case-by-case with Eng approval).

Migration playbook (internal)
- Owner: product-hosted-api + solutions-engineering (SEs).
- Tools to ship: 1) migration-check CLI (detects incompatible calls), 2) automated SDK shim (adds polyfill for common patterns), 3) in-console migration walkthrough.
- Metrics to track: % requests still hitting legacy endpoint, number of successful migrations per week, support tickets opened for migration, and cost delta for migrated customers.
- Timeline:
  - 2026-03-15: Beta migration kit to SEs/CS.
  - 2026-04-01: In-product banner + console guide goes live.
  - 2026-05-15: Legacy endpoint turned off (soft off for 24h with immediate rollback if widespread failures).

Customer-facing FAQ (draft snippets)
- Q: Why are you sunsetting the old endpoint?
  A: To consolidate maintenance and deliver better performance and lower cost. Embeds V2 also unlocks larger-batch processing and better vector consistency.
- Q: Will my vector dimensions change?
  A: In most cases no; we'll include a compatibility run in the migration tool to surface any dim/normalization differences.
- Q: How much effort is migration?
  A: For standard SDK users it's typically a one-line change and a library upgrade. For custom integrations, SE/CS can assist.

Notes-to-self / internal ops details
- Slack channels to notify: #product-announcements, #cs-migrations, #sre-incidents, #private-deployments for customers on VPC.
- Escalation path: SE -> Oncall Eng -> Embeddings PM (Marco) -> Head of Platform (Sophie).
- Risk: legacy clients doing raw HTTP with custom headers may fail; need robust telemetry to catch client error spikes.
- SRE rehearse rollback plan at least twice before sunset date.

Open questions (needs answers before final comms)
- Do we allow automatic server-side routing of legacy traffic to V2 (transparency vs correctness)? (tradeoffs: silent fixes vs potential semantics changes)
- Commitment on emergency extension policy: who approves and what SLAs?
- Final wording for billing implications: will we migrate pricing for legacy customers during the overlap?

Links / references (internal)
- Migration checklist (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Embeds+V2+Migration+Checklist
- Engineering spec: JIRA-INFR-2143
- SDK shim PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/431

Quick timeline for draft comms schedule
- 2026-03-12: Draft internal announcement to PM + CS for review. (this doc)
- 2026-03-19: Finalize customer-facing FAQ + migration guide.
- 2026-03-25: SE/CS training session (internal).
- 2026-04-01: Public in-console banner + docs.
- 2026-05-15: Sunset.

Reminders / quick TODOs
- Add a small demo notebook showing migration for commonly-cited customers (NLP pipeline example).
- Prep a short support library snippet to auto-detect legacy usage and surface an in-app notice.
- Coordinate with pricing ops to confirm no surprise billing changes during overlap.

Draft sign-off owners (who should approve final message)
- PM: Marco Alvarez
- Head of Product: Sophie Patel
- Legal/comms quick check: Devon Brooks

End of scratchpad. Will iterate after PM review.
